questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests for idempotency and long-running behavior are common in search APIs and are easy to misconfigure.

## Key Concepts

- Idempotency keys prevent duplicates
- 202 with Location header enables polling
- Polling strategy and eventual consistency
- Rate limiting and Retry-After handling
- Concurrency: distinct keys yield separate jobs

## Code Example

```python
import httpx

def test_idempotent_search():
    client = httpx.Client()
    payload = {"query": "cpu"}
    headers = {"X-Idempotency-Key": "req-1"}
    r1 = client.post("https://api.example.com/api/v1/search", json=payload, headers=headers)
    assert r1.status_code == 202
    location = r1.headers["Location"]
    r2 = client.post("https://api.example.com/api/v1/search", json=payload, headers=headers)
    assert r2.status_code == 202
    assert r2.headers.get("Location") == location
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test idempotency in a distributed env?
- How to simulate high contention and verify race conditions?

# pseudo compatibility check

    return old_schema.fields.issubset(new_schema.fields) and all(f.optional for f in new_schema.fields if f.name in old_schema.fields)

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Webhook validation is a common integration point with external systems. This tests basic API testing skills (signature validation, error handling), data integrity (idempotency), and ordering under concurrency—practical for production services.

## Key Concepts
- Webhook security (HMAC, timing-safe comparison)
- Idempotent processing with event_id
- Per-merchant data isolation and FIFO processing
- Retry and backoff behavior
- Data-heavy payload handling and timeouts
- CI integration for API tests

## Code Example
```javascript
const crypto = require('crypto');
function verifySignature(body, signature, secret){
  const expected = crypto.createHmac('sha256', secret).update(body).digest('hex');
  return crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(expected, 'hex'), Buffer.from(signature, 'hex'));
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test idempotency storage performance at scale?
- How would you simulate out-of-order event arrival in tests?
